subject.title: [Bug]: default memory hook blocks repeated channel restart recovery

question: Should OpenClaw add host-enforced trigger eligibility metadata to the typed hook contract so restart recovery can safely ignore hooks that cannot run for recovered user turns?
rationale: The proposed fix is a new generic plugin-hook capability rather than a plugin-local bug patch, and maintainers must choose the permanent compatibility and safety contract for existing hook registrations.

options.title: Add a narrow host-owned eligibility contract
options.body: Introduce explicit typed metadata that lets the host prove a hook cannot run for a recovered user turn, while hooks without that proof continue to block recovery.

options.title: Keep the current universal hook gate
options.body: Retain fail-closed behavior for every registered hook and accept resend recovery for this case until a broader hook contract is designed.

options.title: Choose another generic recovery seam
options.body: Keep the memory plugin unchanged but define a different host-level recovery boundary that preserves conservative behavior for third-party hooks.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow host-owned eligibility contract
recommendation.body: Introduce explicit typed metadata that lets the host prove a hook cannot run for a recovered user turn, while hooks without that proof continue to block recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged restart-recovery and repeated-restart QA work provides the closest concrete history for deciding the recovery and hook-contract boundary.
